title: Oracle Against Tyre and Sidon

questions.question: Wail, O ships of what, for Tyre is laid waste, without house or harbor?
Be still, O inhabitants of the coast; the merchants of whom, who cross the sea, have filled you?
And on many waters your revenue was the grain of Shihor, the harvest of the what?
Be ashamed, O Sidon, for the sea has spoken, the stronghold of the what?
When the report comes to Egypt, they will be in anguish over the report about whom?
questions.explanation: Isaiah 23:5 (ESV): "anguish over the report about Tyre."

questions.question: Who has purposed this against Tyre, the bestower of crowns, whose merchants were what?
The LORD of hosts has purposed it, to defile the pompous pride of all glory, to dishonor all the honored of the what?
questions.explanation: Isaiah 23:9 (ESV): "all the honored of the earth."

questions.question: He has stretched out his hand over the sea; he has shaken the what?
The LORD has given a command concerning Canaan to destroy its what?
Behold the land of the Chaldeans! This is the people that was not; whom destined it for wild beasts?
questions.explanation: Isaiah 23:13 (ESV): "Assyria destined it for wild beasts."

questions.question: At that day Tyre will be forgotten for how many years?
questions.explanation: Isaiah 23:15 (ESV): "Tyre will be forgotten for seventy years,"

questions.question: Like the days of one what?
questions.explanation: Isaiah 23:15 (ESV): "like the days of one king."

questions.question: Take a harp; go about the city, O forgotten prostitute! Make sweet melody; sing many songs, that you may be what?
Her merchandise and her wages will be holy to the LORD. It will not be stored or hoarded, but... for abundant food and fine what?
questions.explanation: Isaiah 23:18 (ESV): "for abundant food and fine clothing."

key_verse_text: The LORD of hosts has purposed it, to defile the pompous pride of all glory, to dishonor all the honored of the earth.
